description: issue #775 (review gate, QA finding N7): `wait [ 1 2 ]` -- a tick count that is neither a number nor a word. The corpus pinned only the `number` and `word` arms of `params.actual` for every `expected: "whole number"` diagnostic across the whole stack (`wait`, `every`, `repeat`, `random`), so an implementation could report anything at all for a list or a boolean and still pass the full stack-neutral corpus -- confirmed by mutation. This fixture and its `every` twin (`every/every-non-number-boolean-type-error`, which covers `boolean`) close two of those arms; `wait/wait-non-number-dict-type-error`, `every/every-non-number-record-type-error`, and the turtle pair close the rest, so `params.actual` is now pinned for every `OLTypeName` outside `number`/`word`. Each pins the VALUE too, not just the concept name: the harness unwraps an `OLDict`/`OLRecord` into a plain key->value object before deep-comparing (see the corpus README's "Dict/record contents"), so a dict or record value is genuinely compared. `spec/execution-model.md`'s value model makes `list` and `boolean` first-class Core values, so neither is a degenerate `word` -- and unlike a word there is no coercion rule that could rescue either, so this is `ol-type` outright with no wholeness question to reach. As with every other failed `wait` validation the `primitive` event is NOT emitted (the pause never runs), only the instruction event precedes the diagnostic, and the span covers just the argument.

diagnostics.message: wait needs a whole number, but got a list.
